title: Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations
layout_note: Panel (a) is one left-to-right row of circles and boxes; dashed lines from the bottom corners of the second layer box fan out to the top corners of a wide thin-outlined frame below, panel (b), which opens that layer into two parallel paths.
grouping: Two lettered panels stacked vertically. Colour families by role: the input and output functions a(x), u(x), v(x) are light-blue circles, learned maps (P, Q, R, W) are orange circles, the repeated layers are pale-yellow rectangles, and the closing sum and activation are red-orange circles. In panel (b) the spectral path sits inside a pale-yellow rounded panel of the same fill as the layer boxes in (a); the local path (W) runs below it outside any container. Panel (b) is enclosed by a thin black rectangle titled 'Fourier layer' in its top-right corner.
shapes_depth: Flat filled circles with thin dark outlines for functions and operators; flat pale-yellow rectangles with thin outlines for the layers; no shadows or 3-D. Thin black arrows, straight in (a) and curved in (b). Three large black dots stand for the omitted layers. Between the transform circles sit small line-plot sketches on axes: four stacked sine waves of rising frequency before R, two low-frequency waves after it. Labels are italic serif math inside the circles (a(x), P, R, W, sigma, F and F^-1); layer names are plain sans text.
proposed_highlight: The proposed layer is the only repeated block, drawn in pale yellow, and is the one expanded into panel (b) by dashed zoom lines; its spectral branch reuses the same pale-yellow fill so the zoom reads as the inside of that box.
lesson: Show spectral truncation as data, not a label: put tiny sine-wave sketches between the forward and inverse transform circles, many frequencies before the learned multiplier and only the low ones after it.
notes: Venue read on the PDF first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2021'; venue_source: pdf). The crop includes the explanatory text that the paper sets inside the figure under both panels. The whole figure is one embedded raster in the PDF, so `kb measure` measured all of its pixels (photo_share null) — the palette is the drawing's own colours. Annotation note (2026-11-15): crop also includes the caption text below the figure

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: transformer-stack used loosely for the stack of repeated Fourier layers

core.what: A left-to-right operator chain a(x) -> P -> Fourier layers 1..T -> Q -> u(x) in panel (a), with Fourier layer 2 opened by dashed lines fanning to the corners of a framed detail panel (b) below.

relations.form: panel (a): one horizontal row of circles and boxes, a(x) -> P -> Fourier layer 1 -> 2 -> ... -> T -> Q -> u(x)
two dashed lines from Fourier layer 2's bottom corners to the top corners of the thin-black-framed panel (b); the spectral box in (b) repeats layer 2's pale-yellow fill
in (b) v(x) forks up into the spectral path F -> R -> F^-1 and down through W, and the two curved branches merge at a red '+' before sigma
small sine-wave sketches between F, R and F^-1 show the spectrum before and after the high modes are truncated
the T Fourier layers drawn as layer 1, layer 2, three dots, layer T in the row

channels.colour: light blue = functions a, v, u; orange = learned maps P, Q, R, W; red-orange = sum and activation (near-identical to the learned orange); pale yellow = Fourier layer and its spectral path; F and F^-1 are a lighter yellow-orange
channels.shape: circle = function or operation, rectangle = layer (only in (a)); inside (b) everything is a circle
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow, curved in (b); dashed = zoom callout
channels.frame: thin black frame = the opened Fourier layer; pale-yellow inner box = the spectral path

quality.strengths: The zoom ties the overview to the detail by both geometry (dashed fan-out lines) and matching tint; the spectral-truncation step is drawn as wave sketches rather than only named; both panels read strictly left to right.
quality.weaknesses: Learned maps (P, Q, R, W) and the fixed sum/activation share nearly the same orange, so role colour is hard to read; data (functions) and operations are both circles; the W path bends down and back up in long curves instead of running straight under the spectral box; the crop includes caption text under (b).

insights.structure: Panel (a) is one left-to-right row a(x) -> P -> Fourier layers 1..T -> Q -> u(x); panel (b), a thin black frame below, opens Fourier layer 2 into a spectral path in a pale-yellow box and a local W path below it.
insights.data: Functions a(x), v(x), u(x) are light-blue circles; between F, R and F^-1 small sine-wave sketches show the spectrum before and after truncation of high modes.
insights.emphasis: The spectral path's pale-yellow box repeats the fill of the Fourier layer boxes in (a), and the zoom is signalled by dashed lines fanning from layer 2 to the frame's corners.
insights.flow: Strictly left-to-right in both panels; in (b) v(x) forks up into the spectral box and down to W, and both merge at a red '+' before sigma.
insights.avoid: Using the same orange circle for learned maps P, Q, R and W while the sum and activation are a near-identical red-orange makes role colours hard to tell apart.

arrangement.units: (a) the full architecture as an unframed row; (b) the Fourier layer in a thin-outlined rectangle titled at its top right, stacked below and linked by dashed zoom lines
arrangement.shared: colour roles reused in both panels
